sections.h2: Where do I take a deed or mortgage for recording in Tuscola County?
sections.html:
Find the Register of Deeds in Suite 400 of the Purdy Building, 125 W. Lincoln Street, Caro, MI 48723. It opens at 8:00 a.m. and closes at 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, with a lunch closure from noon until 1:00 p.m., and it shuts for holidays. Call 989-672-3840 or write to registerofdeeds@tuscolacounty.org.

You can walk a document in or send it by post. A mailed packet needs the exact fee and a stamped return envelope. Cash, money orders and checks are all taken. Checks must print both the account holder's name and the bank's name and address, and they cannot be stale-dated. An incorrect amount gets the whole request rejected, so count twice before sealing the envelope.

Caro is the county seat and Vassar is the second city. Tuscola County lies in Michigan's Thumb, about 914 square miles in all with 12% water, and the Tuscola Area Airport serves it along with highways M-15, M-24, M-25, M-46, M-81 and M-138. The county was created in 1840 and organized in 1850.

sections.h2: What are the recording charges in Tuscola County?
sections.html:
A single $30.00 charge covers entering and recording a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, certified copy or other instrument. Papers that discharge or assign several older records add to it.

Tuscola County Register of Deeds fee schedule, taken from the office's Fees for Copies and Recording page
ServiceCharge
Recording one instrument (deed, mortgage, lis pendens and similar)$30.00 flat
Every extra liber and page assigned, discharged, indexed or posted$3.00 extra
Photocopy, real estate record$1.00 a page
Certifying a copy$5.00 a document
Tax lien search certificate, state or federal$3.00 a name

Four dollars of every recording fee funds the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation program. Fixture filings, lien documents, state deeds, plats and tax reversion papers skip that portion. Copies are paid for at the time of purchase, and a mailed order must name the liber and page. Tuscola County also records fixture filings at $30.00, while UCC filings go to the Secretary of State instead of Caro.

sections.h2: Why must a warranty deed visit the Treasurer before it is recorded?
sections.html:
The fee page cites MCLA 211.135 for a rule that taxes must be shown paid before some papers reach the recorder. Three types go to the Tuscola County Treasurer first: warranty deeds, land contract assignments with a warranty clause, and condominium master deeds. The Treasurer's certification costs $5.00 per document.

When the stamped document returns, send it on to Caro in recording order with the exact fee. The Treasurer, at the same street address, answers certification questions at 989-672-3890.

Sellers carrying unpaid tax feel this step most. Settle early with your title company or closing attorney who will order the certificate, since each mailed round trip adds days to a closing.

sections.h2: Which paperwork mistakes get a Tuscola County recording returned?
sections.html:
Staff compare each submission with the list on the office's Recording Requirements page, which starts from MCL 565.201. A document that misses any item comes back to the sender.

  • Original signatures, each with the signer's name typed or printed beneath it. Fax and photocopy versions are refused.
  • An acknowledgement by a notary, judge or court clerk on any paper that conveys or burdens Michigan land.
  • A mailing address for every grantee, plus the name and address of whoever drafted the paper.
  • Black print of 10 points or larger on white paper between letter and legal size, leaving a blank 2 1/2 inches atop page one and 1/2 inch on other margins.
  • No more than four sequential Social Security digits anywhere on the page.
  • One recordable event per instrument, named on the first line of print.

Court orders and death certificates are recordable only as certified copies, and a survivor deed needs the death certificate recorded or referenced by liber and page. Staff do not draft deeds, answer legal questions or hand out blank forms.

sections.h2: What transfer tax is owed on a recorded Tuscola County deed?
sections.html:
Recording a sale brings two charges. The county's is in MCL 207.504: 55 cents per $500 of value, with any leftover under $500 counted as a full unit, for counties below 2,000,000 people. The state's is in MCL 207.525, at $3.75 for each $500 or fraction.

Value must appear on the face of the deed or in an attached affidavit. Tuscola's Recording Requirements page says the whole consideration is taxed unless the paper cites a valid exemption.

  • Both acts exempt consideration under $100, security instruments, leases and certain land contracts.
  • The state act, MCL 207.526, adds conveyances from an individual to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild, plus foreclosure transfers.
  • The county act's list, MCL 207.505, lacks the family exemption. Ask the office how the county share applies when a parent deeds a house to a child.

sections.h2: How can I search or monitor Tuscola County land records?
sections.html:
Online indexes start in December 1988, and the vault holds land records back to 1852 for visitors. Every index is by grantor and grantee name. No search by street address or parcel number exists, and the office cannot tell you a build date, because it keeps land records only.

Copies of recorded documents are open to anyone, since recording makes them public. Residents can sign up for Property Alert, an email notice whenever a paper under their name is recorded. The office calls it an alert, not fraud prevention, and a common name will trigger false alarms. If an alert shows a document you do not recognize, phone the office.

Staff run only simple searches for a small fee and cannot say who owns a parcel. An attorney or title company reaches that conclusion.

sections.h2: What if the property taxes on a Tuscola County house are behind?
sections.html:
The Tuscola County Treasurer works with delinquent owners to head off foreclosure, and its page lays out three paths: keep the property, sell it, or let foreclosure proceed. Forfeiture comes first and is not foreclosure. During it, the county adds a title search fee of at least $175 plus recording costs, and interest climbs to 18% a year (1.5% monthly), reaching back to the start of the delinquency.

A year after forfeiture, foreclosure follows. The owner's interest and every lien are wiped out, redemption ends, and the parcel is prepared for auction. The county says listings usually appear in early August for its August and October auctions. For a bill you dispute, or for a Principal Residence, veteran or poverty exemption, call your township assessor.

A 2025 Census estimate counts 52,680 people over about 805 square miles of land. Homeownership is high at 86.4%, and the 2020 to 2024 median value was $149,500. Households earn a median of $63,811, and workers travel 29.6 minutes on average.

faqs.q: What will a Tuscola County recording cost me?
faqs.a: Expect $30.00 flat per instrument, with $3.00 more for each extra liber and page. Transfer tax comes on top, figured on the total consideration unless the document states an exemption.

faqs.q: Does a Tuscola County warranty deed need a tax certificate first?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the document to the Tuscola County Treasurer first with the $5.00 certification fee, then submit the stamped document to the Register of Deeds with exact recording fees. The Treasurer's phone is 989-672-3890.

faqs.q: Can a Tuscola County deed be found by street address?
faqs.a: No. Indexing is by name only. Search by grantor or grantee, or bring the liber and page, with online indexes starting December 1, 1988.

faqs.q: Who may order a copy of a Tuscola County deed?
faqs.a: Anyone may. Each page costs $1.00, certifying a copy adds $5.00 per document, and a mailed order needs a self-addressed stamped envelope.

faqs.q: Which transfer tax rates apply to a Tuscola County sale?
faqs.a: The county charges 55 cents and the state $3.75, each for every $500 of value. The value comes from the instrument or an attached affidavit.
